implementation_statement: The Lead Systems Engineer creates identity provider accounts on the Operations Manager's request. The RMM tool, hypervisor manager, cloud tenant, DNS account, PSA vault, and colocation access list each keep their own accounts. Gaps: 2 shared RMM support accounts and one shared hypervisor administrator account; a former Support Engineer's VPN account stayed active until 2026-07-22, four months after he left, and he stayed on the colocation access list until 2026-08-18 (P07); no periodic account review.

implementation_statement: The customer portal shows each customer only its own VMs and tickets. Gaps: every RMM technician account can act on all 22 managed customers (no per-customer roles), and every PSA vault entry, including bank server passwords, is readable by all 7 staff.
evidence: Portal role settings; RMM role export; PSA vault permission report

implementation_statement: Gap: one engineer can write, approve, and run an RMM script on every managed customer's servers, and can delete backups. Planned: two-person approval for scripts aimed at more than one customer (2026-11-30) and for backup deletion or retention changes (2026-12-31).

Support Engineers have no cluster or cloud administrator rights. Gaps: the Owner uses standing administrator accounts in the identity provider, cloud tenant, and RMM tool for daily work; the portal's service account has full administrator rights in the hypervisor manager; the PSA vault is open to all staff.
evidence: Role exports from the identity provider, cloud tenant, RMM tool, and hypervisor manager

implementation_statement: The identity provider and RMM tool lock accounts after repeated failed sign-ins (vendor defaults confirmed). Gaps: the customer portal has no lockout or rate limit turned on, and lockout is off on the hypervisor manager's shared local account so that it cannot lock everyone out.
evidence: Identity provider and RMM security settings; portal settings

implementation_statement: All administration is remote. The DC-1 management network is reachable only through the firewall VPN with identity provider MFA. Gaps: the RMM console and the cloud console accept sign-ins from any internet address, and the allowed types of remote access were not documented until POL-02 B.8 (approved 2026-09-15).
evidence: Firewall VPN configuration; RMM and cloud sign-in settings

implementation_statement: All 7 staff completed the vendor's annual awareness module in 2025. Gap: no phishing simulations and no reminders between modules. Planned: quarterly phishing simulations from 2026-11.

Gap: no role-based training for administrators on RMM script safety, verifying callers before password resets, or the bank notice duty. Planned: a 2-hour session for all 5 technical staff by 2026-12-31, then yearly.

provider_if_inherited: MDR provider; RMM vendor; public cloud provider
implementation_statement: The MDR collects identity provider, firewall, and EDR events. The RMM vendor keeps technician and script logs for 30 days; the cloud tenant keeps its audit trail for the provider's default 90 days. Gap: hypervisor manager and BMC logs stay on the devices and roll over in about 7 days; DNS account logs are not kept.
evidence: MDR data source list; RMM log settings; cloud audit trail settings

control_name: Audit Record Review, Analysis, and Reporting
implementation_statement: The MDR reviews the logs it collects, with AI-assisted triage (P10). Gap: nobody reviews RMM, hypervisor manager, cloud tenant, or DNS logs. Planned: a weekly 30-minute review checklist from 2026-10 and MDR ingestion of RMM and cloud tenant logs by 2027-01-31.

The MDR keeps collected logs for 12 months under its contract. Gap: RMM logs (30 days), cloud audit trail (90 days), and device logs (about 7 days) are too short to investigate an intrusion found late. Target: 12 months for management-plane logs.
evidence: MDR contract; RMM and cloud log settings

implementation_statement: An independent IT security consultant assessed 13 controls from 2026-08-17 to 2026-08-19 (P07). POL-02 A.6 requires an independent assessment every year.

Gap: changes to the cluster, network, and RMM policies are announced in team chat with no record, approval, or rollback plan, and maintenance notices go to a customer list that does not include Bank B. Planned: a change log in the PSA with second-engineer approval, and maintenance notices to bank-designated contacts at least 5 business days ahead, by 2026-11-30.
regulatory_driver: Interagency Guidelines III.C.1.d (bank contracts); C-IT-R05 (12 CFR 53.4(b))

implementation_statement: A spreadsheet lists the hosts, storage array, switches, firewalls, and backup appliance with serial numbers. Gap: no inventory of SaaS services, cloud resources, or where bank customer information lives (Bank A's VMs, bank server passwords in the PSA vault). Planned by 2026-10-31.

Gap: no contingency plan or recovery runbook. The BIA (P05) was approved on 2026-09-15. Planned: a short plan covering host and storage failure, loss of DC-1 (restore add-on VMs into the cloud tenant), loss of the DNS account, and hurricane steps, by 2027-03-31.

Customer restores (about 2 a month) succeed but are not recorded, and no planned restore test or recovery exercise has ever run. Planned: quarterly recorded restore tests from 2026-10 and a yearly site-loss exercise.
Gap: there is no second site. Planned: a degraded-mode recovery of add-on VMs into the cloud tenant (SYS-04), tested by 2027-05-31, with customers told in writing which VMs it covers.

provider_if_inherited: Backup software vendor; public cloud provider
implementation_statement: Nightly backups of the 145 add-on VMs (14 days on the appliance, 30 days in the cloud copy), the hypervisor manager configuration, and the portal database. Gaps: the cloud copy is in the same account as the portal and is not immutable; no export of DNS zones; the backup appliance still used the vendor's default administrator password until P07 testing found it (changed 2026-08-19).

A host failure in 2025 was absorbed by the cluster in minutes. Gap: no written procedure to rebuild the hypervisor manager, the storage array configuration, or the portal, and only the Lead Systems Engineer has done it.
Staff use named identity provider accounts for the suite, PSA, MDR console, and VPN. Gap: the 2 shared RMM support accounts and the shared hypervisor administrator account cannot be tied to a person.
evidence: Identity provider user export; RMM technician list

provider_if_inherited: Identity provider vendor; RMM vendor; public cloud provider
implementation_statement: MFA is on for the identity provider (push approval), named RMM accounts, cloud administrator users, and the DNS account. Gaps: the shared RMM support accounts take codes from a seed stored in the team vault, so anyone with vault access can pass MFA; the hypervisor manager and BMCs have no MFA beyond the VPN; push approval has no number matching.
evidence: Identity provider, RMM, and cloud MFA settings; P07 test

implementation_statement: Staff keep credentials in the team password vault. Gaps: the shared RMM password was not changed when a Support Engineer left (rotated 2026-07-23 after the risk assessment found it); BMC passwords have not changed since 2022; the portal's service account password sits in plain text on the portal VM; the backup appliance kept its default password until 2026-08-19 (P07).

Customers sign in to the portal with named accounts. Gaps: MFA is optional (15 of 72 customer administrators use it), and the support desk resets passwords and opens VM consoles on a phone call checked only against the caller's email address.
evidence: Portal MFA report; support desk procedure (interview)

implementation_statement: The P08 runbook (approved 2026-09-15) assigns roles, and the MDR contains endpoint and identity threats. Gap: not yet tested; two incidents in 2025-2026 (a compromised customer VM and a staff phishing click) were handled ad hoc with no records.
evidence: P08 runbook; MDR contract; insurance policy

implementation_statement: POL-03 requires staff to report suspected incidents within 1 hour, and the P08 runbook includes the bank and customer notice steps. Gaps: Bank A's designated contact left the bank in 2024 and Bank B never provided one; staff have not yet been trained on reporting.
evidence: POL-03; P08 notification matrix; bank contact file

implementation_statement: The P08 runbook for compromise of provider tooling serves as the incident response plan at this tier, with contacts and the notification matrix.

Engineers wipe retired hosts with the vendor's tool, but keep no record. Gap: failed storage drives go back to the hardware vendor under warranty with customer data on them (array volumes are not encrypted). Planned: the vendor's keep-the-drive option and certified destruction records, by 2026-12-31.
regulatory_driver: Interagency Guidelines III.C.4 (bank contracts); Fla. Stat. 501.171(8)

implementation_statement: The company keeps its authorized-person list at the colocation provider, a complementary user entity control in the provider's SOC 2 report. Gap: the former Support Engineer stayed on the list until 2026-08-18, and the list is not reviewed on a schedule.
evidence: Colocation access list; P09 vendor review

implementation_statement: DC-1 has badge and biometric entry, cameras, and escorted visitors; the company's racks have their own locks. SOC 2 Type 2 report reviewed 2026-08-26 (P09). The office holds no customer data or servers.

implementation_statement: The Lead Systems Engineer was designated Information Security Lead in writing on 2026-06-15, and the Operations Manager is Compliance Coordinator. Selected by tailoring (not in the Moderate baseline) because both bank contracts ask for a named security contact.
Background checks are completed before hire for all staff, including the 7 current employees.

Gap: no termination checklist; access removal depends on memory (former Support Engineer case). Planned: a last-day checklist covering the identity provider, VPN, RMM, cloud, DNS, PSA, colocation list, and rotation of every shared secret the person knew, by 2026-10-15.
The first risk assessment was completed 2026-07-31 with NIST SP 800-30 Rev. 1 (P01). POL-02 A.2 requires a yearly update.

Gap: no internal vulnerability scanning; vendor advisories are read when someone notices them. Planned: monthly authenticated scans of hosts, BMCs, firewalls, the backup appliance, and the portal VM, a quarterly external scan, and tracking of the CISA Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog, from 2026-11.

Contracts are on file with the colocation, cloud, RMM, PSA, DNS, MDR, and identity providers. The colocation SOC 2 report was reviewed 2026-08-26. Gaps: the RMM and MDR providers have never been reviewed; the RMM contract has no incident notice terms; the MDR contract lets the provider use de-identified telemetry to improve its models.

The colocation bandwidth includes basic upstream DDoS filtering, and the firewalls rate-limit new connections. Gap: no written procedure to null-route an attacked customer address before the shared uplinks fill.
The firewall pair keeps customer VLANs apart and puts the management network behind the VPN. Gap: the BMCs and the backup appliance sit on the same management VLAN that every VPN user reaches.

implementation_statement: TLS 1.2 or higher protects the portal, the API, RMM agent traffic, and the backup copy to the cloud; administrator traffic uses the VPN.
evidence: TLS scan of the portal (2026-07-23); vendor documentation

implementation_statement: The cloud provider encrypts object storage and the managed database by default, and laptops use full-disk encryption. Gap: storage array volumes, including Bank A's VMs, and the backup appliance are not encrypted at rest.

Laptops patch automatically, firewalls quarterly, and the portal software within about 30 days of a release; SaaS vendors patch their platforms. Gaps: the hypervisor hosts are two minor releases behind, BMC firmware has not been updated since 2022, and there are no time limits by severity.
evidence: Host version report; BMC firmware list

implementation_statement: EDR runs on all 9 laptops with 24x7 MDR response. Customer VMs and servers are protected by the customers' own tools under the MSA, except where a managed services contract says otherwise.

The MDR monitors laptops, the identity provider, and the firewalls 24x7 and escalates to the on-call engineer. Gaps: no coverage of the hypervisor manager, BMCs, RMM tool, cloud tenant, or DNS account; the AI triage auto-closes most alerts without anyone at the company seeing them (P10).
evidence: MDR data source list; July 2026 MDR report
